title: TIC quarterly U.S. gross external debt (as-of 2026-09-30) — the missing middle checkpoint, and the series' one 10 a.m. edition
source: EST: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 111,181 bytes) by the tic-quarterly-external-debt-2027-03-31 initial-research adjacency sweep — its 2026 table's December row reads '31' in the column headed 'Quarterly: U.S. gross external debt at end of previous quarter'. The same page's note block gives the rule: 'The release dates are the last business day of each quarter (March, June, September, and December).' Corroborated mechanically: 2026-12-31 is a Thursday and is December 2026's last business day (2027-01-01 falls on a Friday, so no year-end holiday pulls the date earlier), recomputed from 5 U.S.C. 6103 holiday rules rather than a list. THE DATE IS FILED estimate ON MORE THAN THE TAXONOMY, and the reason is specific to December: across all 134 archived Table A vintages fetched and stamped this session, the last-business-day rule reproduces 54 of 59 first-vintage publications at offset +0, but every one of the five exceptions is a June or December release, and three of the five are December (2019-01-31 at +31 during the 35-day funding lapse; 2026-01-16 at +16, flagged '16 (delayed)' on Treasury's own page; 2024-12-30 at -1). The December sub-series runs 12 of 15 at +0 against March's 15 of 15. Treasury's own statistics page singles December out as the one edition released at 10 AM rather than 4 PM. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: DISCOVERED during the tic-quarterly-external-debt-2027-03-31 initial research (2026-09-09), and proposed because it is a HOLE IN THE CALENDAR RATHER THAN A NEW IDEA. tic-quarterly-external-debt-2027-06-30's registered FT-...-2 names three intermediate checkpoints for its 66-for-66 June-revision census — 2026-09-30, 2026-12-31 and 2027-03-31 — and files proposals for only two of them. This is the third. It is also the direct antecedent of the proposing event: it publishes the as-of 2026-09-30 position, the last first vintage observable before 2027-03-31 publishes as-of 2026-12-31, so it is the final input that can move that event's registered level forecast ($31.4tn central, band $30.7tn-$32.1tn). ITS OWN CHARACTER IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE PROPOSER'S. On the census re-run this session, 75 of 75 surviving revision vintages carry a June stamp, so this edition should revise nothing — but it is the FRAGILE edition on schedule (12 of 15 at +0, all three of the series' worst slips) where March is spotless (15 of 15), and the position it publishes, as-of Q3, is restated by a mean 1.265% of level against 0.784% for the as-of-Q4 number the March edition publishes. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds: 16:00 ET (10:00 ET for this edition, per Treasury's statistics page) publication, data a quarter stale, no accompanying press release, no house playbook keyed to a macro release. NOTE THE CORRIDOR: 2026-12-31 is a year-end session with its own index and tax-loss mechanics that own the tape far more than a no-press-release reconciliation statistic. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
